summary: Console widget load latency / 504s when trace-hook request headers exceed 16KB
description:
Issue summary: Several LuminaHealth users report Dashboard widgets failing to render or timing out (504) intermittently when the underlying traces include very large trace-hook header payloads (base64-encoded span attributes).

Impact: Affects multiple dashboard panels that include trace links. Charts either hang in 'loading' state for 15-30s then 504, or render partial data with missing trace links. This prevents on-call and SRE from drilling into traces during incidents and has impacted two production incident investigations in the last 48h.

Environment: Production, us-east-1. Issue started after deployment of trace-hook header expansion change (round-robin agent enrichment) rolled on 2026-03-09. Customer on enterprise plan with Route policy pinned to us-east ingestion.

Observed behavior: When trace metadata headers attached to trace-hook callbacks exceed ~16KB, the console widget requests to /api/console/panel/data show drastically increased latency or 504 errors. Requests with smaller header sizes succeed.

Expected behavior: Console should accept and process trace-hook header values up to the documented limit (32KB) without causing widget-level timeouts or partial renders; large header values may be trimmed by downstream services but should not cause 504s.

Notes: This looks like a regression linked to header forwarding changes in api-gateway/proxy-layer where oversized headers trigger buffering fallback and timeouts in proxy-to-console streaming path.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a trace-hook callback that attaches a large base64-encoded attribute blob (>16KB) to outgoing requests headers (e.g., X-Trace-Meta).
2) Generate a trace that triggers the hook. Confirm the header is present on the ingested trace (via raw events).
3) Open a dashboard panel that queries traces and includes trace-link enrichment. Observe widget loading behavior and backend request timing (browser devtools / network tab).
4) Compare behavior against a control trace with header <1KB.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Confirmed pattern correlates with header size rather than model type or specific dashboard queries.
SRE replicated locally by pushing artificially large X-Trace-Meta header; observed same 15-30s latency then 504 when proxy buffer threshold exceeded.
Proxy change deployed 2026-03-09 reduces in-memory header buffer and switches to disk-buffering for headers >16KB which triggers slower upstream writes and occasional connection resets.
Console backend expects header forwarding and immediate streaming; disk-buffered handoff path does not set Content-Length consistently causing upstream proxies to close connections after timeout.
No evidence of data loss at ingest layer; traces are present, but console-request path fails before join step that attaches trace-links to panel data.
Related config: api-gateway v2.3.1, proxy-layer v1.9.7, console-service v3.4.0.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Ava): Customer reported multiple dashboards returning 504s during incident. Captured sample trace IDs and headers. SLA flagged P1.
2026-03-10 10:03 - SRE (Diego): Confirmed reproduction with synthetic header. Opening INT ticket to track proxy rollback decision. Assigned to Diego for deeper debug.

2026-03-11 08:21 - Customer (LuminaHealth): Additional context - our agents started attaching larger debug blobs for correlating spans after recent rollout; can revert if needed but would prefer a platform fix.

2026-03-11 14:30 - SRE (Diego): Found proxy disk-buffer handshake path does not propagate Transfer-Encoding: chunked header; created minimal patch to set content-length or chunked flag depending on buffer mode. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/1892

2026-03-12 09:05 - Support (Ava): Notified customer of temporary workaround (reduce trace-hook payload size or enable header-trim at agent side). Customer accepted workaround while engineering prepares patch.
next_steps: 1) Backport and roll proxy patch to staging (set Transfer-Encoding: chunked when using disk-buffering) and run synthetic test harness. 2) If fixed, schedule hotfix to prod with canary. 3) Notify LuminaHealth and resume monitoring for 24h. 4) Follow-up: add telemetry to count header sizes and fail-mode occurrences.
notes_for_followup: Add a console-side tolerant path to skip trace-link enrichment if upstream response is in timeout window to avoid full widget 504s; consider trimming header propagation by default for enterprise routes.
